question: Show all city names and the average distance to all other cities.
statements:
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE "city_distance_matrix" AS SELECT "city1_code" AS "city1_code", "city_data_combined" AS "city_data_combined" FROM table_1;
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE "city_metadata" AS SELECT "city_code" AS "city_code", "city_name" AS "city_name", "zhou" AS "zhou", "country" AS "country", "coordinates" AS "coordinates" FROM table_2;

CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE tmp_rows AS
WITH base AS (
  SELECT
    city1_code,
    city_data_combined,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY (SELECT 1)) AS row_id
  FROM city_distance_matrix
),
-- split the long concatenated string by '|'
parts AS (
  SELECT
    city1_code,
    row_id,
    UNNEST(STRING_SPLIT(city_data_combined, '|')) AS part,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY row_id ORDER BY (SELECT 1)) AS part_pos
  FROM base
)
SELECT * FROM parts

CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE tmp_rowcsv AS
WITH merged AS (
  SELECT
    row_id,
    STRING_AGG(TRIM(part), ',') WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY part_pos) AS csv_row
  FROM tmp_rows
  GROUP BY row_id
)
SELECT row_id, csv_row FROM merged

CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE tmp_base AS
SELECT city1_code, city_data_combined,
       ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY (SELECT 1)) AS row_id
FROM city_distance_matrix

CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE tmp_pipes AS
WITH x AS (
  SELECT row_id, city_data_combined,
         regexp_extract_all(city_data_combined, '\|') AS pipes
  FROM tmp_base
)
SELECT row_id,
       UNNEST(pipes) AS pipe_token,
       ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY row_id ORDER BY (SELECT 1)) AS pipe_idx
FROM x

CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE tmp_rowcsv AS
WITH seg AS (
  SELECT row_id,
         string_split(city_data_combined, '|') AS segs
  FROM tmp_base
)
SELECT row_id,
       UNNEST(segs) AS csv_row,
       ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY row_id ORDER BY (SELECT 1)) AS seg_pos
FROM seg

CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE tmp_cells AS
WITH elems AS (
  SELECT r.row_id,
         UNNEST(string_split(r.csv_row, ',')) AS elem,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY r.row_id ORDER BY (SELECT 1)) AS col_pos
  FROM tmp_rowcsv r
)
SELECT row_id, col_pos,
       TRY_CAST(TRIM(BOTH '"' FROM TRIM(elem)) AS DOUBLE) AS dist_val
FROM elems

CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE conductor_s_execution AS
WITH origin AS (
  SELECT pos AS row_id, code AS origin_code FROM tmp_order_final
), dest AS (
  SELECT pos AS col_pos, code AS dest_code FROM tmp_order_final
), joined AS (
  SELECT o.origin_code, d.dest_code, c.dist_val, c.row_id, c.col_pos
  FROM tmp_cells c
  JOIN origin o ON o.row_id = c.row_id
  JOIN dest d ON d.col_pos = c.col_pos
)
SELECT m.city_name,
       AVG(CASE WHEN row_id <> col_pos THEN dist_val END) AS avg_distance
FROM joined j
LEFT JOIN city_metadata m ON m.city_code = j.origin_code
GROUP BY m.city_name
ORDER BY m.city_name NULLS LAST
S:
# Parse matrix without STRING_AGG by deriving row/column positions from delimiters and computing averages.
import pandas as pd

# 1) Assign stable row order (row_id) as input order.
db_api.execute_query(user_id, chat_id, '''
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE tmp_base AS
SELECT city1_code, city_data_combined,
       ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY (SELECT 1)) AS row_id
FROM city_distance_matrix
''')

# 2) Extract positions of '|' delimiters to know row boundaries inside the long string.
# DuckDB supports regexp_extract_all returning list; unnest with positions.
db_api.execute_query(user_id, chat_id, '''
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE tmp_pipes AS
WITH x AS (
  SELECT row_id, city_data_combined,
         regexp_extract_all(city_data_combined, '\\|') AS pipes
  FROM tmp_base
)
SELECT row_id,
       UNNEST(pipes) AS pipe_token,
       ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY row_id ORDER BY (SELECT 1)) AS pipe_idx
FROM x
''')

# 3) Build segments between pipes by splitting on '|' into a list of row CSVs and unnesting with order.
db_api.execute_query(user_id, chat_id, '''
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE tmp_rowcsv AS
WITH seg AS (
  SELECT row_id,
         string_split(city_data_combined, '|') AS segs
  FROM tmp_base
)
SELECT row_id,
       UNNEST(segs) AS csv_row,
       ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY row_id ORDER BY (SELECT 1)) AS seg_pos
FROM seg
''')

# 4) Keep only one segment per row: many datasets place exactly one CSV row between pipes; if multiple, concatenate via SQL replace of '|' beforehand.
# If multiple segs exist, we merge them logically by re-splitting commas across all segs per row.
db_api.execute_query(user_id, chat_id, '''
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE tmp_cells AS
WITH elems AS (
  SELECT r.row_id,
         UNNEST(string_split(r.csv_row, ',')) AS elem,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY r.row_id ORDER BY (SELECT 1)) AS col_pos
  FROM tmp_rowcsv r
)
SELECT row_id, col_pos,
       TRY_CAST(TRIM(BOTH '"' FROM TRIM(elem)) AS DOUBLE) AS dist_val
FROM elems
''')

# 5) Derive city order from input order.
order_df = db_api.execute_query(user_id, chat_id, 'SELECT city1_code AS code, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY (SELECT 1)) AS pos FROM city_distance_matrix')
db_api.register_temporary_df(user_id, chat_id, order_df, 'tmp_order_final')

# 6) Map positions to codes and compute avg excluding diagonal; join names.
db_api.execute_query(user_id, chat_id, '''
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE conductor_s_execution AS
WITH origin AS (
  SELECT pos AS row_id, code AS origin_code FROM tmp_order_final
), dest AS (
  SELECT pos AS col_pos, code AS dest_code FROM tmp_order_final
), joined AS (
  SELECT o.origin_code, d.dest_code, c.dist_val, c.row_id, c.col_pos
  FROM tmp_cells c
  JOIN origin o ON o.row_id = c.row_id
  JOIN dest d ON d.col_pos = c.col_pos
)
SELECT m.city_name,
       AVG(CASE WHEN row_id <> col_pos THEN dist_val END) AS avg_distance
FROM joined j
LEFT JOIN city_metadata m ON m.city_code = j.origin_code
GROUP BY m.city_name
ORDER BY m.city_name NULLS LAST
''')
